comments.author: milesial
comments.body:
What are you trying to achieve? The 6th feature you are extracting here is the proton number, which is an invariant scalar (1D). Here you are passing this scalar as a type-1 feature which is for 3D vectors, and the model expects a 3D vector so it errors as it should.

Multiple input types are supported if they are defined correctly

comments.author: milesial
comments.body:
Yes, for point cloud experiments using +z, I suggest data loading code like this:

```
G = dgl.transform.knn_graph(points, self.num_neighbors + 1)
G = dgl.transform.remove_self_loop(G)
src, dst = G.edges()
absolute_z = points[:, -1]

# position relative to neighbors
relative_pos = points[src] - points[dst]
relative_z = relative_pos[:, -1].clone()
relative_pos_no_z = relative_pos.clone()
relative_pos_no_z[:, -1] = 0
feat = torch.stack([relative_pos, relative_pos_no_z], dim=1)
edge_feats = {'0': relative_z[..., None, None], '1': feat}
node_feats = {'0': absolute_z[..., None, None]}
G.edata['rel_pos'] = points[dst] - points[src]

return G, node_feats, edge_feats, label
```

With the model defined with:
```
fiber_in=Fiber({0: 1}),
fiber_edge=Fiber({0: 1, 1: 2}),
```

That way you have two 3D edge features: one vector and one vector with z=0. You also have one 1D edge feature: the relative z component. You have one 1D node feature: the absolute z component.

You can find more insight in this discussion about ScanObjectNN https://github.com/FabianFuchsML/se3-transformer-public/issues/13
